title: Determination of Forward and Futures Prices: Part 2
prerequisites: Spot-forward parity F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT) from Chapter 5 Part 1
Continuous dividend yields and cost of carry
Foreign exchange spot rate quoting conventions
learningOutcomes: Distinguish between forward contract value f and forward delivery price during contract life.
Calculate the mark-to-market value of an existing forward contract using f = S_t - K*e^(-r(T-t)).
Price stock index futures using continuous dividend yield q and identify index arbitrage opportunities.
Analyze why index arbitrage broke down during the October 1987 Black Monday market crash.
Apply covered interest rate parity to calculate forward exchange rates and execute FX arbitrage.
Explain how storage costs and convenience yields determine contango vs backwardation in commodity markets.

sections.title: The Mid-Life Valuation Dilemma
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Establish the distinction between forward delivery price and contract value prior to maturity.
keyPoints: Forward price F_0 is agreed delivery price when contract value is zero.
As spot prices move, existing contracts accumulate positive or negative market value f.
Long contract value equals spot minus discounted delivery price: f = S_t - K*e^(-r*tau).

sections.title: Stock Index Futures & Index Arbitrage
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate index futures pricing F_0 = S_0*e^((r-q)T) and program trading cash-and-carry bounds.
keyPoints: Index dividend yield q continuously offsets financing costs.
F_0 > S_0*e^((r-q)T) triggers automated basket buying and futures shorting.
F_0 < S_0*e^((r-q)T) triggers automated reverse cash-and-carry.

sections.title: The October 1987 Crash: When Arbitrage Broke Down
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Dissect Snapshot 5.4 to explain portfolio insurance cascades and NYSE DOT system order jams.
keyPoints: Dynamic portfolio insurance hedgers flooded CME with massive S&P 500 futures sell orders.
Futures traded at huge discounts to cash index quotes.
Arbitrageurs could not execute because NYSE DOT order printers lagged by hours, freezing liquidity.

sections.title: Currency Forwards & Covered Interest Rate Parity
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Derive F_0 = S_0*e^((r - r_f)T) and execute step-by-step covered interest arbitrage.
keyPoints: Foreign interest rate r_f acts as a continuous dividend yield.
Forward exchange rate depends on the interest rate differential (r - r_f).
Divergence generates instant riskless covered borrowing and FX conversion profit.

sections.title: Commodities: Storage Costs & Convenience Yield
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate F_0 = S_0*e^((r + u - y)T) to define contango vs backwardation.
keyPoints: Storage cost u increases forward carrying cost.
Convenience yield y reflects operational security of holding physical inventory.
When y > r + u, market flips into backwardation (F_0 < S_0).

misconceptions.misconception: An existing forward contract always maintains zero value until its final expiration day.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Forward contracts have zero value only at initiation. Mid-life spot changes create mark-to-market value f = S_t - K*e^(-r(T-t)).

misconceptions.misconception: Stock index futures trade at pure spot compounding without adjusting for stock dividends.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Index portfolios pay dividends, which continuously reduce the cost of carry: F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)T).

misconceptions.misconception: Commodity futures must always trade at a premium to spot prices due to storage and financing costs.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: During physical shortages, the convenience yield y exceeds storage and interest costs (y > r + u), driving futures below spot into backwardation.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A long forward contract on a non-dividend stock has delivery price K = $50 with 3 months remaining (tau = 0.25). The spot price is $53 and the continuous risk-free rate is 6%. An analyst calculates contract value.
activeRecallQuiz.question: What is the theoretical mid-life value f of this long forward contract?

coreTakeaways: Mid-life forward value f = S_t - K*e^(-r*tau) discounts the agreed delivery price against current spot.
Stock index futures pricing F_0 = S_0*e^((r-q)T) continuously credits dividend yields against financing carry.
In the 1987 crash, index arbitrage broke down when NYSE DOT execution bottlenecks disconnected futures from spot.
Covered interest rate parity F_0 = S_0*e^((r - r_f)T) guarantees foreign currencies price interest rate differentials.
Convenience yield y measures physical inventory utility, allowing commodity markets to invert into backwardation.
